title: Rivian's LiDAR-Equipped R2 to Reach Customers in 2027 as Autonomy Rollout Begins
detail: Rivian announced that its LiDAR-equipped R2 SUV will reach customers in 2027, with employees receiving the vehicle this year as part of the company's broader autonomy rollout. The integration of LiDAR hardware into the mass-market R2 signals Rivian's push to deliver advanced driver-assistance and autonomy capabilities at a more accessible price point.

media.caption: Rivian R2 with LiDAR autonomy hardware

title: BMW Unveils 2027 i3 with Up to 468 Miles of Range
detail: BMW unveiled the 2027 i3 with a maximum range of up to 468 miles, confirmed at a premium price tier. The announcement marks a significant leap in range for the revived i3 nameplate and reinforces BMW's commitment to long-range electric vehicles as competition in the premium EV segment intensifies.

media.caption: BMW 2027 i3 electric vehicle with 468-mile range

title: Tesla Solar Factory Caught in Patent War Between Chinese Suppliers Linton and Jingsheng
detail: Tesla's solar factory has been drawn into a patent dispute between Chinese suppliers Linton and Jingsheng, complicating the company's solar supply chain. The conflict between two key Chinese equipment manufacturers highlights the growing legal risks embedded in EV and solar supply chains as competition among Chinese component makers intensifies.

media.caption: Tesla solar factory affected by patent dispute between Chinese suppliers

title: Workhorse Lands Fresh 200-Truck Commercial EV Order Signaling Demand Growth
detail: Workhorse announced a new commercial order for 200 electric trucks, signaling continued demand growth in the commercial EV segment. The order reinforces momentum for fleet electrification as commercial operators increasingly commit to zero-emission vehicles ahead of tightening emissions regulations.

title: Ford's $30,000 Fathom EV Pickup Production Launch Faces Uncertainty
detail: Ford's planned $30,000 Fathom EV pickup truck faces production launch uncertainty ahead of its scheduled rollout. The affordable truck had been positioned as a key entry-level electric offering, and delays or cancellation could affect Ford's competitiveness in the high-demand affordable EV pickup segment.

title: Toyota Drops 1,675 lb Caravan on Electric Truck to Demonstrate EV Durability
detail: Toyota released a promotional video showing its electric truck surviving a 1,675 lb caravan drop test, demonstrating structural durability in a dramatic stress scenario. The stunt highlights Toyota's push to counter perceptions that electric trucks lack the ruggedness of traditional combustion-engine workhorses as competition in the electric truck market heats up.
